name: get_memory_map
description: Pinned process VMAs, coalesced page-state ranges or fixed address cells. Plain pagemap fallback leaves huge/written/zero unknown; NUMA is optional VMA totals only (numa=true). Cells require a range, retain unmapped gaps, and distinguish virtual-category changes from PMD mapping changes; physical migration is unknown. Pagination requires the returned cache.sequence after page one; a changed publication returns StaleMemorySnapshot. Reads one shared background cache at most once per second; first call may be pending. Four live process/range scopes, bounded scans, explicit partial/unavailable states. No target memory reads, dirty-bit resets, policy changes, or physical frame numbers. Expensive collection adapts refresh_ms toward 0.8% of one core per scope (maximum 60 seconds); requests may continue at 1 Hz. Inspect cache age and cost_limited; page-scan CPU/range bounds can separately report partial coverage.

cell_bytes.description: Cells only: 2097152 (default) or host base page size. Range boundaries must align.

redact.description: Hide process names, VMA paths and inodes in this reply. Virtual addresses and pinned PID identity remain.

numa.description: Collect per-VMA NUMA totals; adds a numa_maps walk. Omitted by default.

name: get_thp_state
description: System-wide THP/khugepaged settings, zswap and vmstat counter deltas; optional pinned process smaps/rollup totals and eligible PMD coverage. Supply pid and start_ticks together. Counters never attribute kernel activity to a selected process. Reads one shared background cache at most once per second; first call may be pending. Four live process/range scopes, bounded scans, explicit partial/unavailable states. No target memory reads, dirty-bit resets, policy changes, or physical frame numbers. Expensive collection adapts refresh_ms toward 0.8% of one core per scope (maximum 60 seconds); requests may continue at 1 Hz. Inspect cache age and cost_limited; page-scan CPU/range bounds can separately report partial coverage.

name: get_fragmentation
description: Linux buddy free blocks per zone/order and kernel fragmentation index. -1000 means a suitable allocation exists; other negative indices are valid. Zero free pages is separately visible. This index is not a completion percentage. Includes system-wide counter deltas. Reads one shared background cache at most once per second; first call may be pending. Four live process/range scopes, bounded scans, explicit partial/unavailable states. No target memory reads, dirty-bit resets, policy changes, or physical frame numbers. Expensive collection adapts refresh_ms toward 0.8% of one core per scope (maximum 60 seconds); requests may continue at 1 Hz. Inspect cache age and cost_limited; page-scan CPU/range bounds can separately report partial coverage.
